messages.subject: [statnet_help] ERGM problem
messages.body_plain:
Hello Narciso,

The error is strange, and not one I've seen before.  Can you let us know 
which version of the ergm package you are using?  We just uploaded a new 
one to CRAN a week ago.  If you are using an old one, you should try the 
newest first: upgrade to R 3.0.0 as well, and then all your packages 
with either update.packages() or with update.packages("name.of.package") 
for each of the statnet packages.  Let us know if the error is still there.

That said, from the evidence I am seeing, it would appear that your 
particular model is likely to be degenerate.  I can tell this by the 
fact that the log-likelihood improvements keep going back up to the 
maximum cap (around 20). That may not be the result you want, but it is 
still an informative about the fact that this model is not the right 
generative model for your data.  It doesn't explain the error though.

Cheers,
Steve

messages.subject: [statnet_help] commands from ergm tutorial take too long to complete
messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] commands from ergm tutorial take too long to complete
messages.body_plain:
Hello Szabolcs,

Indeed, with that set of versions you had, it appears that the tutorial 
does go into silence for a long time there.  As you figured out, this is 
a result of the fact that this case is pathological, although the way it 
was handled then was not ideal.

The good news it that with the latest versions of the packages (which 
just went up on CRAN a week ago) we have instituted some more 
informative checks on degeneracy that return much faster.  If you 
install those, you'll see that after just 5-10 seconds you'll get an error:

Error in ergm.MCMLE(init, nw, model, initialfit, control = control, 
MHproposal = MHproposal,  :
   Number of edges in a simulated network exceeds that in the observed 
by a factor of more than 20. This is a strong indicator of model 
degeneracy. If you are reasonably certain that this is not the case, 
increase the MCMLE.density.guard control.ergm() parameter.

This means that you get a very quick indication that there is almost 
certainly a problem, but also have a means of overriding it and 
continuing the fit if you so desire.

Alas, with the software always evolving and improving, the old versions 
of tutorials will get out of date in their behavior. More good news: 
each year we upgrade a set of core tutorial materials for the INSNA 
Sunbelt Conference to work with the latest versions of the packages.  
These will available on the statnet website each year shortly after the 
conference (ie some time in late spring).

Cheers,
Steve

messages.subject: [statnet_help] error with custom ergm terms
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am using ergm with custom written terms.  The term works well when used on its own, and produces correct results: ergm(nw ~ myterm)

Unfortunately when I use it together with other terms (ergm(nw ~ myterm + kstar(2))), I often, but not always, get an error like this:

Error in if (order) coefs[order, seq_len(order)] else numeric() : 
  argument is not interpretable as logical

The error comes up only after a number of iterations have finished without problems.
Sometimes there's also a warning like this:

In if (order) coefs[order, seq_len(order)] else numeric() :
  the condition has length > 1 and only the first element will be used

Does anyone have any ideas what this might be caused by?  I found references to the same error in the mailing list archive, but no tips on why this might happen.  Unfortunately I am having trouble reproducing the problem with a *simple* example (so I wouldn't have to post the full code for my term as well as the full data).  I'd still appreciate even some vague hints on what may be happening here.

I have the latest version of R and ergm that are available from CRAN.

Best regards,
Szabolcs Horv?t

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Here is some additional information on this problem.  Perhaps someone can give me some hints on what may be going wrong based on this.

Here's the traceback() when the error is issued:

8: ar.yw.default(x, aic = aic, order.max = order.max, na.action = na.action, 
       series = series, ...)
7: ar.yw(x, aic = aic, order.max = order.max, na.action = na.action, 
       series = series, ...)
6: ar(x[, i], aic = TRUE)
5: spectrum0.ar(x)
4: effectiveSize(x)
3: approx.hotelling.diff.test(esteq, esteq.obs)
2: ergm.MCMLE(init, nw, model, initialfit, control = control, MHproposal = MHproposal, 
       MHproposal.obs = MHproposal.obs, verbose = verbose, response = response, 
       ...)
1: ergm(faux.magnolia.high ~ myterm + kstar(2),
       control = control.ergm(MCMLE.maxit = 20, MCMC.runtime.traceplot = T), 
       verbose = T)

With verbose=T, the error happens just before "Average estimating equation values:" would be printed for this iteration.

The very last "traceplot" shown before the "crash" (with MCMC.runtime.traceplot = T) is flat. (This has to be an artefact of the "crash", right?)

If I use MCMLE.maxit to stop the iteration just before ergm() would "crash", and then run mcmc.diagnostics on the resulting fit object, I get the same error (mcmc.diagnostics() gives the same error).

If I examine this fit object, and generate some samples using simulate(), it appears to fit the input data very well.  There's no sign of degeneracy.  (I also expect this based on theoretical considerations.)

My custom term may produce very large changestats.  They may be as large as several hundred for this particular network.  Does the magnitude of the changestats matter?  (Rescaling them won't help.)


Based on these observation I have the impression that it is not the core fitting algorithm that runs into trouble and causes the error, but something else.  Is there a way to disable the part of ergm() that causes the problem?

Best regards,
Szabolcs Horv?t

messages.subject: [statnet_help] statnet changelog?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Szablocs,

Statnet the package did just updated, but indeed there was a version 
number change that went with it, although it's an easy one to miss: from 
3.0.1 to 3.1.0. Also, it's still propagating through the mirrors so 
depending on where you grabbed it from yesterday you might have gotten 
the old one or the new one. Statnet the package is very simple; 
essentially all it does is "depend" on the latest versions of the 
packages in the statnet suite, such that it's an easy way to install and 
load all of them at once. So the only change to it was to update version 
numbers on other packages.

Yours,
Steve

I am new to social network analysis so I apologize in advance if the
question below is without interest for most of you...

I have recently used the sna and statnet package to calculate the

It worked fine when I did it a couple of month ago but when I wanted to
implement the procedure again today, I was puzzled with the dyad.census
function. The output of this function had "0" Null dyad for matrices
containing plenty of null dyads, the command is.na in these matrices showed
appropriate results.

I have tried with a hypothetical matrix:

#Matrix for 5 inds.: 1 Null dyad, 1 Mutual dyad

vec<-c(NA,1,1,1,NA,0,NA,1,1,1,0,0,NA,1,1,0,0,0,NA,1,NA,0,0,1,NA)

g=network(ex,directed=T)
ndyad<-dyad.census(g); ndyad

     #Mut Asym Null
#[1,]   1    8    0
